name: Equilibra
description: Equilibra is a comprehensive neurochemical rebalancing agent designed for users who have been on multiple substances over extended periods and whose baseline brain chemistry has drifted so far from normal that they no longer know what 'normal' feels like. It uses a slow-acting SNT-mediated multi-system recalibration approach — simultaneously adjusting dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine, GABA, and glutamate systems toward statistical population baselines over a 6-month course. Lazarus markets it as 'returning you to yourself.'
effects: Gradual restoration of baseline affect and cognition
side_effects: First month: profound uncertainty as unfamiliar baseline states emerge
Identity disturbance — some users report not recognizing the person they're becoming
Interferes significantly with most other psychoactive substances
Expensive enough that missing doses causes inconsistency problems
Rare: recalibration overshoot — landing outside normal parameters in unpredictable directions
duration: 6-month course; effects are intended to establish permanent new baseline
cultural_context: Equilibra is a Lazarus prestige product — sold to Tier 3 and 4 recovery clients with the implicit promise that you can buy back the person you were before addiction. The identity disturbance side effect is poorly advertised: many users discover that their 'baseline' self is someone they don't like or recognize. Recovery counselors debate whether this is a side effect or the point — the person who developed the addiction is also being recalibrated away.
story_hooks: A character three months into Equilibra is genuinely becoming someone different — old relationships, loyalties, and skills are shifting — and someone in their life wants to stop the process
A Lazarus data leak suggests the 'statistical population baseline' Equilibra targets has been quietly adjusted — whose definition of normal is being installed?
Someone needs to be themselves — their drug-altered self — for a specific mission, but they're mid-course on Equilibra and losing access to the person they need to be
